target_customer: Defense, intelligence, mining, infrastructure, insurance and AR and autonomy customers needing 3D Earth data
problem: Accurate 3D data of the Earth is expensive to collect. Array Labs flies clusters of small radar satellites in formation to build high-resolution 3D models.
business_model: Radar satellite data and capacity contracts, plus radar sensors and elevation datasets

founders.name: Andrew Peterson
education: BS and MS in Aerospace Engineering
founders.background_notes: YC page: led remote sensing teams including work on the Vera Rubin Observatory, satellite constellation design and radar imaging.

founders.name: Jose Isaac Robledo
founders.background_notes: YC page: business development and financial analysis helping close over $500M in investments.

competitors.name: ICEYE
competitors.traction_then: Established SAR provider with NRO contract in 2022
competitors.funding_then: $136M new funds in 2022 per Nanalyze, totals conflict across sources

competitors.name: Umbra
competitors.funding_then: $44.6M total after $32M raise per a 2021 Nanalyze update

technical_complexity.rationale: Formation-flying radar satellite clusters with custom radar panels need aerospace and RF breakthroughs plus launch access.

defensibility.rationale: Capital intensity, flight heritage, defense relationships and radar IP create high barriers, though funded SAR rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Umbra and Raytheon teamed with Array Labs on 3D imaging in January 2025, so a rival became a partner.

market_need_then: Defense and commercial buyers were funding SAR constellations, with NRO awarding commercial SAR contracts to five companies in 2022. The launch post says accurate 3D data is expensive to collect.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, capability focused; claims such as 60x image quality improvement

branding.community_and_virality: Space trade press covered funding and partnerships. A Creative Director brand job posting suggests brand guideline work.

brand_strength.rationale: Space trade coverage exists but no press on the brand itself; name echoes the antenna array concept.

outcome_analysis: Array Labs raised a $5M seed in October 2022, a $20M Series A in January 2026 led by Catapult, and reported a $21M strategic round anchored by Mitsubishi Electric in mid-2026. It has multi-year capacity contracts and government work, but its first formation-flying launch has slipped to mid-2027 per Aviation Week. Outcome depends on a hardware launch and defense demand.
notes: Founding year not stated on YC page; aggregators say 2021 or 2022. A $10M round in 2024 appears in one search summary only, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round; total of $35M cited at Series A does not reconcile cleanly with the rounds listed. The $21M round is stated by Pulse 2.0, Evertiq, Defense Post and Tectonic Defense; stage unstated so labeled other. Competitor sources: SAR rivals taken from 2021 to 2022 dated pieces; Umbra funding is from a 2021 update. Headquarters Palo Alto, Redwood City or Sunnyvale across sources.
